frames.narration: A checkout request reaches the frontend. Its tracing library creates a trace id, 4bf92f35..., and a first span, 00f067aa..., for the request. Nothing is sent anywhere yet.
The frontend calls the payment service and the library adds a header, traceparent: 00-4bf92f35...-00f067aa...-01. The final 01 says this trace is being recorded. No other work is added to the call.

The payment service reads the header and starts a child span with the same trace id and the frontend span as its parent. After 2.0 s its call to the bank times out, the span is marked as an error, and the finished span is appended to an in-memory queue in microseconds.

states.pay: child span: error after 2.0 s, buffered

frames.narration: The frontend gets the failure and ends its own span after 2.4 s, also with an error. Each service's library now holds a span in a bounded buffer, and the request has already been answered without waiting for any tracing system.

states.front: span ended: error after 2.4 s, buffered

frames.narration: In the background, each library sends its batch to the agent on its host, every 2 s or 512 spans. If the buffer were full because the backend was slow, spans would be dropped and counted instead of blocking anything.

The agent forwards to a collector, which routes by a hash of the trace id so every span of this trace goes to the same tail sampler. The payment span arrived first and its parent second, which is fine because the tree is built later.

After the 10 s wait the sampler decides with the whole trace in front of it. Both spans have an error, so the trace is kept. About 98 of every 100 ordinary traces are dropped here, and 2 of 100 are kept as a baseline.

The store writes both spans under the trace id and adds index entries for service payment, status error, operation charge and duration 2.4 s. Within about 30 s of the request ending, the trace can be found.

A customer complained, so an engineer searches for service payment, status error, in the last hour. The index returns a short list of trace ids. A trace id taken from a log line would go straight to the trace's partition.

The store reads the trace's spans and builds a tree from the parent ids. The engineer sees the frontend span of 2.4 s, with the payment span of 2.0 s below it ending in a timeout, and a link to the logs of that span.
